items.title: Pensions and benefits services still down after 'cyber incident'
items.summary: The UK's former chief technology officer says the Department for Work and Pensions may have been hit by hackers, but the government has not confirmed that.

items.title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip
items.summary: The Princess of Wales has made a documentary, Heal, describing her cancer experience in her own words.

items.title: Two staff killed in Israeli strike on Gaza medical clinic, MSF says
items.summary: The Israeli military says it targeted "Hamas terrorists" in the strike which has been condemned by the World Health Organization.

items.title: Pharmacies get new powers to swap prescriptions during shortages
items.summary: If a medicine is out of stock, staff can offer the same drug in a different strength or form, like a capsule instead of a pill.

items.title: Set time aside for children to read for pleasure, schools to be told
items.summary: The government says its new cirriculum hopes to reverse declining literacy rates and combat "mindless scrolling".

items.title: Charity founded in Captain Tom's name bids to be struck off
items.summary: The charity is now known as the 1189808 Foundation, having dropped the late fundraiser's name.

items.title: Australian wrestler Bronson Reed dies aged 38, WWE says
items.summary: Tributes have flooded in for the 38-year-old Australian who is survived by his pregnant wife, Paige, their daughter.

items.title: ‘Everything under one roof you didn't even know you needed’: Is this the end for Poundland?
items.summary: With baskets loaded full of bargains, shoppers at the much-loved chain tell the BBC the high street doesn't need more empty shops.
